Why I let AI agents change my OS only through Nix
AI agents make it trivial to change your operating system and hard to remember what they changed. Here's why I manage NixOS and macOS from one Nix config in Git.
A browser tool that puts every carousel photo on the same white mat, like a gallery print

Instagram can keep each photo's original aspect ratio in a carousel, but I prefer a white canvas with even borders. I built a page that pads every image onto one shared canvas, entirely in the browser.
Getting Handy speech-to-text to type on NixOS and COSMIC, and to use my eGPU
Handy's shortcut did nothing, and after I fixed that, nothing got typed. A Wayland shortcut, a microphone, the paste method and an autostart file caused it, and the GPU did not.
Getting a Razer Core X eGPU to work after login on NixOS, without timing the boot
My Razer Core X eGPU only worked if I timed it against boot. On NixOS the NVIDIA driver rejected the hotplugged card; PCI kernel parameters and a device node fixed it.
Stop stashing half-finished work: use Git worktrees and Worktrunk
Git worktrees keep separate branches checked out at once. Worktrunk automates per-worktree setup. The same isolation also works for parallel AI agents.
